contradictions: 01_koncepcja F12: 'R 0,5 Ω bocznikowany K_R (normalnie zamknięty)' and §4 'stan bezpieczny = brak zasilania cewek'. If K_R is a NO contactor energised to keep the bypass closed, loss of control power (E-STOP, watchdog, blown B6) INSERTS the 0.5 Ω resistor permanently under 32 A (512 W, no time limit) = fire. Must be an NC pole (energise-to-insert-fault). Same inversion risk for K_N, K_L3, K_PE, K_Tbyp wherever '2P 40 A normalnie zamknięty' was meant as 'coil energised in normal'.

PE pole: faults lens says 'NC pole of a 25-40 A contactor, PE closed when de-energised'; gear lens recommends industrial AC-3 contactors (Chint NC1, LC1D) for durability and mirror contacts - but industrial contactors have NO main poles only. Resolution: PE uses a MODULAR contactor NC pole(s) (Hager ESC228 2NC / ESC428 2NO+2NC class, Noark Ex9CH25 02/22, Eaton Z-SCH230/25-22, F&F ST25-22) with both NC poles in PARALLEL for restore-redundancy (acceptable here because PE carries no current normally; the gear lens' objection to parallel poles concerns current sharing), plus diverse feedback (R5).

Toroid switching sequence: 01_koncepcja says 'najpierw zamknąć gałąź T1, potem otworzyć bocznik'; faults lens says 'bypass must be closed before any changeover'. BOTH create a moment where the energised secondary is short-circuited by the bypass contact (winding in parallel with a closed contact) -> transformer short circuit, 600-1100 A through a 40 A modular contact -> weld, then B6 trips. Neither sequence is safe with an energised primary. See R19 (switch the primary, not the secondary, or de-energise the primary during every overlap).

Pro 3EM placement: shelly lens = supply-side reference meter; metering lens = on the OUTPUT after K_SEQ/K_L3 to 'confirm' faults; but Pro 3EM voltage inputs are rated 100-260 V and Shelly Pro supply 110-240 V, while F10b boost reaches 254-278 V and F4 neutral shift reaches 300-400 V. Output-side placement destroys the meter in exactly the demos it is meant to confirm. Resolution R34.

Guard RCD: 01_koncepcja fixes 'RCD strażnik 300 mA typ S'; faults lens offers 30 mA B vs 100-300 mA 'document the choice'. A 300 mA S device does NOT protect a person: in F16 (PEN break) the chassis/EV body sits at ~230 V and a person draws 150-230 mA (IEC 60479 ~1-1.5 kΩ) - inside the 150-300 mA 'may or may not trip' band, and type S adds 130-500 ms delay. The 300 mA S is fire/backstop protection only. Resolution R12.

01_koncepcja F16 'tylko po 2-krotnym potwierdzeniu na HMI' vs 01 §4 'wszystko, co dotyczy bezpieczeństwa, jest sprzętowe'. A touchscreen double-confirm is not a safety measure (no diversity, no positive action, defeatable by firmware bug/network). F16 needs a hardware enabling device (hold-to-run) and barrier, R14.

Boost magnitude: 01 proposes +48 V (278 V) '[?]'; faults lens limits to +15 % (≈265 V) for ≤30 s; Shelly/Pro 3EM inputs 240/260 V max; typical universal SMPS rating 264 V. Polish grid often 235-245 V at light load, so even +30 V can give 265-275 V. Resolution R18: firmware picks the tap from the MEASURED supply so the output never exceeds 260 V.

F15: 01 says 6 mA DC injection 'nie da się z rozdzielnicy'; faults lens proposes a DC ladder at 'injection point A = DUT output / Type 2 socket'. Both are right only if point A is on the VEHICLE side of the wallbox (through a Type 2 breakout/adapter); an L->PE path at the switchboard output terminals is UPSTREAM of the wallbox RDC-DD and will not test it. Also smooth DC through an upstream Type A guard RCD blinds it (R28).

Loose contact: shelly lens proposes mJS-scripted chatter of a contactor coil from a Shelly; gear lens requires ≥100 ms pulses, ≤30 cycles per burst, industrial contactor; faults lens recommends a 40 A SSR in the 32 A path derated to 20 A. An SSR has negligible I²t withstand and fails shorted; a Shelly script cannot be interlocked by hardware. Resolution R23/R24: industrial contactor in the 32 A path driven by the ESP32/Modbus relay inside the key/E-STOP chain; SSR only on the 16 A single-phase branch with its own fuse.

Door hardware: gear lens lists 230 V AC pilot lamps (AD16-22DS 230 V) and 230 V coil circuits via Shelly on the door-adjacent HMI; hmi/enclosure lenses put a SELV ESP32 board 15 mm deep in the same steel door. Mixing 230 V door devices with a SELV HMI harness in a door opened for demos is poor practice; R36 moves all door devices to 24 V PELV.

Enclosure lens recommends steel because of 'bonded metal body for PE-fault demonstrations' - the enclosure body must NEVER be part of any PE-fault demonstration; it stays hard-bonded to the supply PE at all times (R37). Steel is still right, but for IK10, heat and shielding, not for 'PE demos'.

gear lens: use the 2nd pole of each 2P 40 A contactor as a 24 V position feedback. Acceptable only if the 24 V circuit is treated as PELV (earthed, same insulation class as 230 V) - adjacent poles of a modular contactor are insulated for 400 V between phases, not for SELV separation. Prefer dedicated auxiliary-contact blocks or optocoupled 230 V sensing.

Enclosure sizing: 02_dobor_obudowy reserves ~7 modules for metering; metering lens says 14-17 modules + a 150x60 mm CT bar; safety adds 4-6 modules (second guard RCD option, shunt trip, timer/watchdog relays, door-switch terminal, 2 A fuses for voltage taps). Total DIN count is nearer 120-130 modules, which supports 1000x800x300 and argues against 800x600.
safety_concerns: R01 CLASSIFICATION: Build, document and label the unit as electrical TEST EQUIPMENT per EN 50191 (VDE 0104) operated only by qualified persons (SEP E ≤1 kV), not as a PN-HD 60364 / PN-EN 61439 distribution board. Reason: IEC 61851-1 8.4 and HD 60364-5-54 543.3.3 forbid any switching device in PE in an installation; only a test installation with a key-enabled test mode may do it. Deliverables: nameplate 'URZĄDZENIE PROBIERCZE - SYMULATOR USTEREK - PE MOŻE BYĆ ODŁĄCZONY', ISO 7010 W012 sign, instrukcja stanowiskowa, ocena ryzyka, commissioning protocol (PE continuity, Zs, RCD test) kept with the unit.

R02 FAIL-SAFE PRINCIPLE (energise-to-fault): every fault element must be inserted by ENERGISING a coil and removed by DE-ENERGISING it: PE path through NC pole(s), N path through NC pole, L3 path through NC pole, resistor bypass through NC pole, toroid bypass through NC pole, RCD-bypass through NO pole (so de-energised = RCD in circuit), N-PE/L-N swap through 2NO+2NC changeover with the NC pair = correct wiring. Loss of control voltage, E-STOP, watchdog, thermostat, door switch or blown control fuse must all return the output to CORRECT wiring. Only the main output contactor (K_SEQ pair) is energise-to-run.

R03 PE SWITCHING SCOPE: switch ONLY the single DUT PE conductor between the 'PE wyjściowe' block and the DUT terminal. Never switch the enclosure PE bar, the supply PE, the control-circuit PE, the heatsink/plate bonding or the PE of any instrument. Keep a separate 'PE sieciowe' bar (hard-bonded body, plate, door, heatsink, CT bar shrouds) and a 'PE wyjściowe' block (DUT only).

R04 PE POLE RATING: the NC pole(s) carrying DUT PE must withstand the prospective L-PE fault current at the DUT for the upstream C32 clearing time (TN final circuit ≤0.4 s). Use two NC poles of a 25-40 A modular contactor in PARALLEL (redundant restore) and verify the contactor's conditional short-circuit rating Iq with the C32 (UNVERIFIED - request datasheet). Minimum PE conductor to DUT 6 mm² (available) because F5/F6/F13 can route up to 32 A continuously through it.

R05 PE VERIFICATION (diverse feedback): before the HMI shows 'PE OK' the controller must see (a) the K_PE auxiliary contact 'closed', (b) U(DUT-PE vs supply-PE) < 5 V from an isolated sensor (ZMPT101B-class module through 2x100 kΩ + fuse, or opto-detector), and (c) during PE-open tests the same sensor must show the expected voltage. A mismatch for >500 ms = FAULT_ERROR: drop all coils, open main contactor, red lamp, require key reset. Do not trust a modular contactor's aux contact alone (not a mirror contact per IEC 60947-4-1 Annex F - UNVERIFIED for specific models).

R06 E-STOP: red mushroom on yellow, latching, positively-opening NC contact (e.g. Spamel ST22-B / XB4BS8442 class) wired in series with the 24 V (or 230 V) coil supply of ALL fault contactors AND the main output contactor pair -> output off, PE/N/L restored, resistor and toroid bypassed. Second NC/NO block reports to ESP32. E-STOP acts without any software.

R07 E-STOP REDUNDANCY against a welded main contactor: add a second, independent break - either (a) two contactors in series on the output (K_main + K_SEQ pair) or (b) a shunt-trip/undervoltage release on the main MCB or switch (Hager MZ203, Eaton Z-ASA/230, Schneider iMX A9A26476, Noark Ex9 shunt trip - names from memory, UNVERIFIED on Allegro). Weld detection: Pro 3EM/ESP32 current > 0.5 A while output commanded OFF for > 1 s -> fire the shunt trip and latch.

R08 TEST-MODE KEY: all coils that can alter PE, N, L-N, N-PE, RCD-bypass and voltage are fed ONLY through: key switch 'TRYB TESTOWY' (key removable in OFF, held by instructor) -> E-STOP NC -> door-switch NC (R09) -> heatsink thermostat NC (R21) -> hardware watchdog relay (R10) -> maximum-duration timer (R10) -> Shelly/Modbus/ESP32 relay. A network command (Shelly RPC, Modbus) alone can never open PE.

R09 DOOR POLICY: either (a) steel door kept CLOSED during every test, with a door-position switch in the coil chain (open door -> faults removed, output off; instructor override only with a second key) or (b) transparent/glazed door so nothing needs opening; and in both cases IPXXB finger-safe inside (R38). Opening a live 400 V test board in front of trainees is otherwise an EN 50191 'test station without protection against direct contact' and demands barriers and a second qualified person.

R10 HARDWARE WATCHDOG + MAX-DURATION TIMER (firmware-independent): ESP32 outputs a 1 Hz heartbeat to a retriggerable off-delay relay (2 s); no heartbeat -> coil supply off. In series, a one-shot ON-duration timer relay limits any PE-group / N-group fault to ≤60 s per activation and F16 to ≤10 s; re-arm requires the key to be cycled or an enabling button released. Timer-relay models (F&F PO-/PCU- series) UNVERIFIED.

R11 SHELLY DEAD-MAN: every Shelly Switch.Set that inserts a fault must carry toggle_after ≤ 30 s (Gen2+) / timer (Gen1) and be re-armed by the HMI every 10 s; HMI or Wi-Fi death -> Shelly reverts. This is an ADDITIONAL layer; it never replaces R06-R10 because Shelly relays are NO general-purpose 16 A contacts with no positive guidance and are reachable over the network.

R12 GUARD RCD DECISION (ranked question 1): if ANY person may touch the DUT, its cable, an AmpCheck or a connected vehicle during PE/N/PEN/no-RCD demos, the non-bypassable guard on the feed MUST be 30 mA Type B (instantaneous) - a 300 mA S guard will not reliably trip at the 150-230 mA a person draws from a 230 V chassis and adds ≥130 ms delay. If the user insists on 300 mA S (to show 'nothing trips without RCD'), then F13/F16/F5/F6 are HANDS-OFF demos behind a barrier with no real EV, documented as such. Compromise worth offering: 100 mA Type B instantaneous (trips 150-230 mA within 150 ms; ignores the 34 mA F14 step).

R13 F13 (RCD BYPASS) RESTRICTIONS: K_RCDbyp coil in the key chain; bypass permitted only with guard per R12; FORBIDDEN together with F1, F2, F3, F16 (open/high-Z/live PE without any residual protection = chassis at 230 V indefinitely) and with F4 (N open + no RCD + N-PE paths). Allowed with F5, F6, F14 (that is the didactic point) but F5/F6 without RCD put up to 32 A through the DUT PE/vehicle PE for the whole demo - limit to ≤30 s and ≤16 A load.

R14 F16 (PEN BREAK = F1+F4+F6) is the only permitted COMPOSITE fault and the most dangerous: chassis and EV body at ~230 V. Conditions: hardware hold-to-run enabling button (fault exists only while the instructor holds it, max 10 s by timer), guard per R12, no real EV, DUT behind barrier, red lamp + buzzer, 'ZAKAZ DOTYKANIA' sign, both hands of trainees visible. No touchscreen-only confirmation.

R15 REAL VEHICLE: forbid connecting a real EV during F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, F13, F16 (vehicle body becomes an exposed-conductive-part at up to 230 V with no RCD). Use AmpCheck / EV simulator as the 'vehicle'. A real EV is acceptable for F4 (1-phase only), F7, F8, F9, F10 (within R18), F11, F12, F14.

R16 DUT MOUNTING: the WB500 must NOT be screwed to the enclosure, its door or any bonded metal; mount it on an insulated panel (HPL/PE plastic ≥10 mm, or wood) with ≥0.5 m to the enclosure, so its chassis is earthed only via the switchable DUT PE conductor and never via mounting screws (which would both defeat F1 and carry F3 voltage onto the enclosure).

R17 N-OPEN (F4): with a 3-phase DUT the L-N voltage can swing to 300-400 V (neutral shift). Rule: F4 is allowed (a) on the single-phase 16 A branch, or (b) on the 3-phase output only after K_L2/K_L3 have opened (3-phase DUT then merely loses power) unless the 'DUT SACRIFICIAL' flag is set by key; the neutral-shift demo with two unequal heaters (1 kW/2 kW -> 267/133 V) only in sacrificial mode, ≤5 s, never with F10b, and never with any 230 V instrument (Pro 3EM, Shelly, voltage relays) referenced to the output N.

R18 OVER-VOLTAGE LIMITS (F10b): maximum output 260 V L-N at the DUT, duration ≤30 s, then ≥60 s pause; firmware selects the boost tap from the MEASURED supply voltage (if U_supply > 236 V use the +24 V/+12 V tap, if > 248 V refuse boost) so that U_out ≤ 260 V always; +48 V (278 V) is FORBIDDEN (exceeds 264 V universal-SMPS rating of DUT electronics, Shelly 240 V, Pro 3EM 260 V). Buck down to 182 V is harmless to electronics; limit by demo need only. Boost on L1 only; never combine F10b with F4, F5, F6, F16, F13.

R19 TOROID SWITCHING (series winding in L1): never close the bypass contact across an ENERGISED secondary - that short-circuits the transformer (estimate 600-1100 A for a 1 kVA toroid with uk 3-5 %, UNVERIFIED) and welds a 40 A modular contact before B6 trips. Recommended: switch the PRIMARY instead of the secondary: NORMAL = secondary bypass closed, primary open; sequence = close primary-short contactor (secondary becomes ~0.03 Ω, drop ≈1 V @32 A) -> open bypass (no dropout) -> open primary-short, 20-50 ms dead time -> close K_buck or K_boost (primary fed anti-/in-phase, ~4.3 A). Reverse to restore. Hardware interlocks: K_buck/K_boost mutually excluded (mechanical + NC aux); bypass coil AND primary-short coil both pass through NC aux of K_buck and K_boost (bypass can never close and primary can never be shorted while the primary is fed). If the secondary-side design is kept, the primary MUST be de-energised during every overlap and the DUT accepts a ≥50 ms dropout at each step.

R20 TOROID PROTECTION: primary via B6 1P + NTC/soft-start (inrush 20-50x In); varistor S14K275 across the primary; secondary conductors ≥6 mm² rated for the C32 let-through; a downstream short during boost sends the full fault current through the winding - acceptable for <0.1 s but fuse-protect the primary against reflected current. Toroid mounted with the insulated centre-bolt kit (no shorted turn through the mounting plate), ≥50 mm from the resistor hot zone.

R21 RESISTOR BANK (F12) THERMAL: 0.5 Ω at 32 A = 512 W, 1 Ω at 32 A = 1024 W. Hardware: 4x 1 Ω/100 W Al-housed resistors on a heatsink ≤0.5 K/W (fan-cooled), housings bonded to PE, KSD301 85-90 °C NC bimetal in the K_R coil chain (energise-to-insert, so a hot heatsink REMOVES the fault), DS18B20/NTC to ESP32 (block above 75 °C), one-shot thermal fuse 120 °C as last line. Firmware duty: 0.5 Ω -> ≤60 s @16 A (128 W) with ≥120 s cooldown, ≤10 s @32 A; 0.25 Ω -> ≤30 s @32 A (256 W); 1 Ω only on the 16 A branch. Silicone (SiHF) wiring in the hot zone, 'GORĄCA POWIERZCHNIA' label, PVC wires ≥50 mm away.

R22 RESISTOR SHORT-CIRCUIT COORDINATION: with 1 Ω in series a downstream bolted fault gives only ≈200 A, which may NOT reach the C32 magnetic threshold (160-320 A) -> thermal tripping in seconds while 40 kW is dumped into the resistor. Therefore the 1 Ω step is allowed only behind B16 (magnetic 48-80 A), and the 0.5/0.25 Ω steps (≈420/≈800 A) behind C32. Alternatively fuse the resistor branch with gG 32 A.

R23 LOOSE CONTACT (F11) with contactor: use an industrial AC-3 contactor (Chint NC1-3210 class, mirror/aux block) not a modular one; min OFF 100 ms, min ON 500 ms, ≤30 operations per burst, ≥2 min between bursts, hard cap 50 000 cycles then replace (cycle counter in NVS); re-closing onto an EV OBC can draw 50-100 A inrush, so AC-3 making capacity matters. Weld detection (aux contact or current while commanded OFF) -> open main contactor. Never chatter K_PE, K_N, K_RCDbyp or any changeover pair.

R24 SSR (if used for F11): only on the 16 A single-phase branch, genuine 40 A zero-cross part derated to ≤20 A, heatsink (≈1.2 V x 16 A ≈ 19 W), MOV + RC snubber, own gR/aR fuse or B16 (SSR I²t is tiny and it fails SHORTED or ruptures); bypass contactor in parallel so SSR off-state leakage (mA) and failure do not matter; never in the 32 A path, never for PE/N.

R25 N-PE SWAP / BRIDGE (F5/F6): implement F5 with one 2NO+2NC changeover contactor (break-before-make, mechanical exclusivity) - never two independent contactors; dead time ≥50 ms. F6 bridge relay 16 A. Both FORBIDDEN with F1/F2/F3 (PE open + swap = chassis at 230 V) and with F4 (N open + swap = load returns through PE indefinitely). Allowed with F13 only under R12/R13.

R26 L-N SWAP (F7): the single-phase outlet must have its OWN N conductor and N block (never share N with the 3-phase output - a swap on a shared N would put 230 V on the 3-phase DUT's N and 400 V L-N on it) and 2-pole (1P+N switched) overcurrent protection, because after the swap the 'N' conductor carries L. Use one 2NO+2NC changeover contactor. Forbidden together with F4, F5, F6.

R27 AC LEAKAGE LADDER (F14): resistors 38k/23k/15k/7.7k/3.8k Ω (6/10/15/30/60 mA) wirewound/ceramic rated ≥3x dissipation (25 W for the 30 mA step) and ≥500 V; each step through its own 0.5 A fuse; injection only L1->DUT-PE at the switchboard output (point B) for upstream-RCD demos; switched by Shelly/relay 16 A contacts (AC, fine). Forbidden together with F2 (100 Ω in PE -> 0.5 W, ok, but no RCD trips and PE sits at 3-6 V) only when F13 is also active.

R28 DC LEAKAGE LADDER (F15/'blinding'): switch on the AC side of the bridge rectifier - Shelly and most 16 A relays are rated 240 VAC / 30 VDC and will NOT break 325 V DC; bleeder 100 kΩ across the 10-47 µF capacitor (stored 0.5-2.5 J, hazardous per IEC 61010 >0.35 J); guard RCD must be Type B because smooth DC blinds a Type A guard too; DC steps ≤30 mA; after the demo verify the upstream RCD still trips (test button) before continuing.

R29 RDC-DD TEST POINT: 6 mA DC/AC injection meant to exercise the wallbox's own RDC-DD must be applied on the VEHICLE side of the wallbox (Type 2 breakout/adapter, as AmpCheck does), not at the switchboard output; the switchboard ladder tests the installation RCD only. Label the two points differently on the HMI.

R30 HIGH-IMPEDANCE PE (F2, 50-200 Ω): resistor ≥50 W wirewound rated ≥500 V, bonded heatsink; a bolted L->chassis fault without RCD would dissipate 230²/100 Ω = 530 W in it with the chassis at 230 V indefinitely -> F2 FORBIDDEN with F13, F3, F6, F14 >6 mA; permitted only with the 30 mA installation RCD in circuit (fault clears in <40 ms, pulse energy ≈21 J).

R31 PE LIVE (F3): only via ≥220 kΩ (≈1 mA) or an isolated 24-50 V/≤10 VA source + ≥4.7 kΩ; resistor ≥1 W rated ≥500 V in two series parts, 0.1 A fuse; permitted only with F1 active (PE open) and never with F5/F6/F13; the DUT, AmpCheck and anything bonded to DUT PE are to be treated as live (1-10 mA is perceptible, not lethal).

R32 CONTROL SUPPLY: ESP32 PSU, Shelly supplies, coil supply, fan and instruments are fed from the SUPPLY side (after main switch and guard RCD, before any fault element) through their own 2-6 A MCBs; control N and control PE are never switched; nothing that the controller needs may be referenced to the output N or output PE (otherwise F4 kills the controller mid-fault).

R33 SHELLY LIMITS (user wants stocked units used): allowed roles = coil drivers for non-safety-critical contactors inside the key/E-STOP chain, leakage-ladder AC switching (<1 A), metering (Pro 3EM, EM-50) and status inputs. Forbidden = any 32 A load path (16 A general-purpose contacts), any DC >30 V, any safety interlock, any device downstream of boost/N-open (240 V supply rating), direct PE switching, driving coils from a channel on another phase (Pro 4PM/Pro 2PM/1PM share L). Configure voltage_limit 280 V / undervoltage_limit 0 / power_limit off on PM units; disable the Shelly AP, disable cloud, enable digest auth or keep the LAN physically isolated; use dry-contact models (Pro 1/2/3, Plus 1, 1 Gen3) for 24 V coil circuits and common-L PM models only for 230 V coils on L1.

R34 MEASURING-DEVICE PLACEMENT: Pro 3EM voltage taps after the K_SEQ pair but BEFORE the toroid, resistor, SSR, K_N and PE block (sees sequence/phase loss/supply voltage, never 260-400 V), via a 3P+N 2 A MCB; CTs on the supply CT bar. Output-side voltages (boost, neutral shift, PE voltage) only through isolated transducers scaled for ≥400 V (ZMPT101B with divider) into the ESP32 and a 400 V-rated 3-phase monitoring relay (F&F CKF-B/CP-730 class); any device downstream of fault elements must be rated ≥300 V continuous. Smart meter (Eastron/ORNO, 80-100 A direct) sits in the same upstream position.

R35 SPD only on the SUPPLY side (before all fault elements); a T2 varistor (Uc 275 V) downstream of boost or neutral shift conducts, overheats and thermally disconnects. If the DUT has an internal SPD it is at risk during F4 - part of the 'sacrificial' decision.

R36 DOOR & HMI VOLTAGES: all door-mounted devices (E-STOP, key switch, enabling button, lamps, buzzer, door switch) on 24 V DC PELV from a DIN PSU; HMI (5 V SELV) harness segregated from 230/400 V by ≥10 mm air or separate duct, no Dupont wires, strain-relieved loom across the hinge; do NOT fit a Li-ion cell to the Waveshare board's charger inside a hot 400 V enclosure; RS485 to Modbus relay modules is the only long run from the HMI.

R37 BONDING: enclosure body, mounting plate, door (flexible green-yellow braid across the hinge, ≥4 mm² - EN 61439-1 figure UNVERIFIED), gland plate, resistor heatsink, toroid bracket, CT-bar shrouds and switch frames hard-bonded to the supply PE bar; the DUT PE terminal is the ONLY switchable PE; commissioning test: PE continuity <0.1 Ω to every bonded part, documented.

R38 IPXXB INSIDE: every live terminal reachable with the door open is finger-safe (terminal covers on contactors and MCBs, shrouded CT bar, insulated resistor terminals, covered toroid lugs, enclosed leakage ladders), so that an opened door exposes no live part even in fault states; mark fault-switching zone with 'MOŻE BYĆ POD NAPIĘCIEM PRZY OTWARTYM PE'.

R39 COIL SUPPRESSION & CONTACT PROTECTION: RC snubber (100 Ω + 100 nF X2) or MOV S10K275 across every 230 V coil and a flyback diode/TVS across every 24 V coil driven by Shelly/relay-board contacts (otherwise contact erosion and ESP32 resets); coil wiring 0.75-1.0 mm² H05V-K with ferrules; each coil group on its own 2-4 A fuse.

R40 MUTUAL-EXCLUSION MATRIX (controller + where possible hardware): groups PE{F1,F2,F3}, N{F4,F5,F6}, L{F7,F8,F9}, V{F10a,F10b}, Z{F11,F12}, RCD{F13,F14,F15}; at most ONE fault per group; forbidden pairs: F10b+F4, F10b+any PE, F10b+F13, F13+any PE, F13+F4, F1/F2/F3+F5/F6, F4+F5/F6/F7, F9 change while output live, F11+F12, F12(1 Ω)+32 A path; only permitted composite: F16 (R14). Phase-sequence swap only with output de-energised (both K_SEQ open ≥100 ms).

R41 MAXIMUM DURATIONS (firmware, backed by the hardware timer of R10): F1/F2/F3 ≤60 s; F16 ≤10 s hold-to-run; F4 1-phase ≤60 s, F4 neutral-shift ≤5 s; F5/F6 ≤30 s; F10b ≤30 s then ≥60 s pause; F10a ≤120 s; F11 bursts ≤30 ops; F12 per R21; F13 ≤120 s; F14/F15 ≤30 s; auto-restore and 'return verified' before the next arm.

R42 ARMING PRECONDITIONS: output current <1 A for any PE/N/L/changeover switching (break-before-make under load erodes contacts and exposes the DUT to transients); DUT idle for F9; heatsink <60 °C for F12; supply voltage 207-253 V and correct sequence (Pro 3EM) for any test; all aux contacts reporting 'normal'; key in TEST; door closed; no E-STOP latched.

R43 RETURN-TO-NORMAL VERIFICATION before the HMI shows 'OK': all aux contacts in normal state, U(DUT-PE vs PE) <5 V, output L-N voltages 207-253 V on all phases, N current plausible, RCD-in confirmed; if the guard or installation RCD tripped, the HMI must demand a manual reset and a test-button check.

R44 NETWORK/ACCESS: the touchscreen alone must never be sufficient to create a hazardous state - key (R08) + hold-to-run (R14) are physical; isolated LAN/Wi-Fi with WPA2 and static IPs; Shelly AP disabled; no Internet; firmware 'instructor PIN' is convenience, not safety.

R45 OUTPUT OUTLET: if a CEE 32 A 5P socket is used, label it 'TYLKO URZĄDZENIE BADANE - PE PRZEŁĄCZANE' and energise it only in test mode via the key; otherwise fixed terminals in a covered box. Prevents a trainee plugging a drill into an outlet whose PE may be open.

R46 LOCKOUT & STORED ENERGY: padlockable main switch (rozłącznik 63 A) for maintenance; DC ladder capacitor bleeder (R28); toroid de-energised when key OFF; label 'Przed otwarciem odłączyć zasilanie i odczekać 10 s'.

R47 THERMAL SUPERVISION: filter fan + grille drops the enclosure to IP54 -> indoor use only; internal air sensor: >45 °C blocks F12 and F10, >55 °C removes all faults and alarms; fan run-proof via temperature trend or current; baseline dissipation (coils + Shelly + PSU + toroid no-load) ~60-100 W must be included in the enclosure heat calc.

R48 PRE-SESSION SELF-TEST (automatic, 30 s): verify PE closed (R05), all faults off, output voltages/sequence normal, E-STOP and door switch functional (operator presses, controller confirms coil supply dropped), installation RCD test button pressed by operator and trip confirmed. Log results on SD with timestamp.

R49 WEIGHT/MOUNTING: 1000x800x300 steel with plate is 50-60 kg empty, ~80-90 kg equipped (toroid 7-10 kg, contactors, resistors); wall anchors rated accordingly (≥4x M10 into structural wall or a floor stand); door-mounted HMI adds leverage - keep hinge-side mass low.

R50 WHAT MUST STAY IN HARDWARE vs FIRMWARE (summary for the synthesizer): hardware = energise-to-fault wiring, key, E-STOP (+shunt trip), door switch, watchdog relay, max-duration timer, heatsink thermostat, mechanical/NC-aux interlocks of all changeover pairs and toroid contactors, guard RCD, SELV/PELV segregation, bonding; firmware = exclusion matrix, durations, preconditions, feedback comparison, tap selection from measured voltage, cycle counters, logging, Shelly toggle_after.
questions_for_user_ranked: 1. Czy podczas pokazów 'brak PE', 'PE pod napięciem', 'zamiana N-PE', 'brak RCD' i 'przerwa PEN' ktokolwiek (kursanci, Ty) będzie dotykać ładowarki, jej kabla, testera AmpCheck lub podłączonego auta? Czy do pokazów podłączane będzie PRAWDZIWE auto, czy symulator (AmpCheck)? Od tego zależy, czy RCD 'strażnik' na zasilaniu musi być 30 mA typ B (chroni człowieka, ale czasem wyzwoli razem z RCD 'instalacyjnym'), czy może zostać 300 mA S (nie chroni człowieka - pokazy wyłącznie 'bez dotykania', za barierą).

2. Jakie dokładnie modele i ilości Shelly są w magazynie (Pro 3EM 120A/3CT63, Pro EM-50, Pro 4PM, Pro 3, Pro 1/1PM, Pro 2/2PM, Plus 1/1PM, 1 Gen3, Plus Uni, Wall Display, EM Gen3)? Czy akceptujesz zasadę, że Shelly sterują tylko cewkami styczników i mierzą, a nic związanego z bezpieczeństwem (PE, E-STOP, blokady) nie przechodzi przez Shelly ani przez sieć?

3. Czy WB500 i P35 użyte na stanowisku to egzemplarze 'do zużycia' (dopuszczasz ryzyko uszkodzenia elektroniki przy 260 V lub przesunięciu punktu zerowego do 300-400 V), czy mają pozostać sprawne? Masz ich karty z dopuszczalnym zakresem napięcia wejściowego i informacją, czy mają RDC-DD 6 mA, kontrolę N-PE/PEN i kolejności faz?

4. Kto będzie obsługiwał stanowisko (uprawnienia SEP E do 1 kV?) i czy chcesz, żeby było formalnie udokumentowane jako urządzenie probiercze (instrukcja stanowiskowa, ocena ryzyka BHP, protokół pomiarów przed uruchomieniem)? Czy pokazy odbywają się w jednym miejscu (sala szkoleniowa) czy w terenie u klientów?

5. Jaki jest układ sieci w miejscu pokazów (TN-S czy TN-C-S i gdzie jest rozdział PEN), jakie zabezpieczenie przed rozdzielnicą (bezpiecznik/MCB, prąd) i przewód zasilający (np. YKY 5x10 mm²)? Czy możesz zmierzyć impedancję pętli zwarcia w punkcie przyłączenia?

6. Czy przepięcie może być ograniczone do max 260 V (krok +12/+24/+30 V dobierany automatycznie od zmierzonego napięcia sieci), tylko na L1 i tylko na ≤30 s? Czy pod/przepięcie ma działać przy 32 A (toroid 1000 VA 2x12 V lub 1500 VA na zamówienie, 7-12 kg) czy wystarczy przy 16 A (800 VA 2x24 V)?

7. Czy drzwi mają być otwierane podczas pokazu pod napięciem (wtedy wyłącznik drzwiowy w łańcuchu bezpieczeństwa i pełne osłony IPXXB w środku), czy wystarczą drzwi przezroczyste / okno i drzwi zamknięte podczas testu?

8. Czy pokaz 'przepalonego styku' ma być realnie termiczny do kamery termowizyjnej (rezystory do 512 W, radiator z wentylatorem, kratki = IP54, tylko wnętrza) czy wystarczy sam spadek napięcia zrobiony transformatorem (zero ciepła)?

9. Czy wstrzykiwanie upływu DC 6 mA (test RDC-DD ładowarki, 'oślepienie' RCD typu A) jest w zakresie? Wymaga adaptera Type 2 po stronie pojazdu, RCD strażnika typu B i przełączania po stronie AC prostownika.

10. Wyjście do ładowarki: gniazdo CEE 32 A 5P (wygoda, ale ryzyko podłączenia obcego odbiornika przy otwartym PE) czy stałe zaciski/puszka tylko dla DUT? Czy ładowarka będzie montowana na osobnej płycie izolacyjnej ≥0,5 m od obudowy (konieczne), a nie na obudowie?

11. Czy jedna usterka naraz (plus jedyna dopuszczona kombinacja F16 = brak PE + przerwa N + mostek N-PE, na przycisku podtrzymania ≤10 s) jest akceptowalna dydaktycznie, czy chcesz innych kombinacji? Każda dodatkowa kombinacja wymaga osobnej analizy.

12. Czy budżet dopuszcza dodatkowe elementy bezpieczeństwa: wyzwalacz wzrostowy do wyłącznika głównego (redundancja E-STOP), przekaźnik watchdog i przekaźnik czasowy limitu trwania, drugi stycznik główny, czujniki napięcia izolowane na wyjściu (łącznie ok. 400-800 PLN, do weryfikacji)?
enclosure_recommendation: Safety view confirms the enclosure lens: steel wall enclosure 1000x800x300 mm, IP66/IK10, full galvanised mounting plate, two bottom gland plates (Rittal AX 1180.000 ~1582 PLN on Allegro per enclosure lens, Adelid OM1008030 1649 PLN as fallback); 800x600 is too small once the metering zone (14-17 modules), the safety additions (shunt trip, watchdog/timer relays, second guard RCD option, 2 A tap fuses, door-switch terminals, ~4-6 modules) and the hot zone are counted (~120-130 modules + toroid + resistor bank + CT bar). Safety requirements on the box itself: (1) body, plate, door (flexible bonding braid across the hinge), gland plates, heatsink, toroid bracket and CT-bar shrouds hard-bonded to the SUPPLY PE - the enclosure is never part of any PE demonstration; (2) the DUT (WB500) mounted on a separate insulated panel ≥0.5 m away, never on the enclosure; (3) door: steel door with the 7-inch HMI and ONLY 24 V PELV door devices (E-STOP, key 'TRYB TESTOWY', hold-to-run enabling button, lamps, buzzer) plus a door-position switch in the coil chain; if 'seeing the contactors' is wanted, choose a factory glazed door (Legrand Atlantic 036949 class, 2100-4400 PLN, not on Allegro) and keep it closed during tests - do not plan on opening a live door in front of trainees; (4) interior zoning: A = supply/protection/metering (top-left, incl. CT bar with shrouds), B = fault-switching 230/400 V contactors (middle), C = hot zone (resistor bank + fan + toroid) top-right next to the outlet grille with silicone wiring, D = SELV/PELV (ESP32 PSU, Modbus relay modules, Shelly LAN switch) bottom, separated by ducts/partition ≥10 mm; (5) IPXXB finger-safe everywhere reachable with the door open (terminal covers, shrouded busbars, insulated resistor terminals); (6) ventilation: 150x150 filter fan low + 223x223 filtered outlet high (enclosure lens parts) with KTS 011 thermostat and ESP32 temperature supervision -> IP54, indoor only; without the thermal F12 demo, natural convection suffices (ΔT ≈14 K at 150 W); (7) padlockable main switch, EN 50191 nameplate and ISO 7010 W012 warning on the door, red 'USTERKA AKTYWNA / PE ROZŁĄCZONE' and green 'STAN NORMALNY' lamps visible from the trainee side; (8) mounting: 80-90 kg equipped -> ≥4x M10 anchors into a structural wall or a floor stand; keep the hinge-side mass low because of the door-mounted HMI.
architecture_recommendation: Power path order (fixed by safety): input terminals (10 mm²) -> CT bar (4 straight 6-10 mm² runs L1 L2 L3 N, ≥100 mm, ≥40 mm pitch, shrouded) for AC500 DLB CTs and Shelly Pro 3EM CTs -> padlockable main switch 4P 63 A -> guard RCD (30 mA Type B if hands-on possible, else 300 mA S or 100 mA B - user decision) -> SPD T2 (supply side only) -> main output contactor pair = reversing pair for F9 (Chint NC1-3210 class with mechanical interlock) optionally plus shunt-trip on the main MCB for E-STOP redundancy -> Pro 3EM voltage taps and optional RS485 smart meter via 3P+N 2 A MCB -> MCB 3P C32 (3-ph) and 2-pole B16 (1-ph branch with its OWN N) -> RCD-select block (Type AC/A/B 30 mA via break-before-make selector + bypass contactor NO, de-energised = RCD in) -> fault section: K_INT (industrial contactor, L1) -> SSR (16 A branch only) -> resistor bank with NC bypass -> toroid section with NC bypass and PRIMARY-side buck/boost/short contactors -> K_L2/K_L3 (NC poles) -> K_N (NC pole) -> PE block (2x NC poles in parallel, 100 Ω relay, 220 kΩ relay, N-PE bridge relay) -> changeover 2NO+2NC contactors for N-PE swap and L-N swap -> output terminals / CEE 32 A (key-enabled) and 1-ph outlet. Leakage ladders (AC steps L1->DUT-PE; DC ladder switched on the AC side of its rectifier) at the output; vehicle-side RDC-DD injection only via a Type 2 adapter. Control architecture: ESP32-S3 7-inch HMI (Waveshare) as supervisor/state machine; RS485 Modbus RTU relay module (Waveshare RTU Relay D, 8 relays + 8 DI) for timing-critical faults (F11 bursts, changeovers) and aux-contact read-back; stocked Shelly devices (per user: use what is in stock if it fits) for slow on/off coil drivers and leakage ladders (dry-contact Pro 1/2/3/Plus 1 for 24 V coils, common-L Pro 4PM/1PM for 230 V coils on L1 only), Pro 3EM as upstream reference meter + phase-sequence flag + Switch Add-on as extra trip, Pro EM-50/EM Gen3 with clamps on output N and output PE for N/PE current, Plus Uni for low-voltage glue; every Shelly fault command with toggle_after ≤30 s re-armed by HMI. All coils fed through the HARDWARE safety chain: key 'TRYB TESTOWY' -> E-STOP NC (+ second NC/NO to ESP32, + shunt trip) -> door switch NC -> heatsink thermostat NC -> watchdog relay (ESP32 heartbeat, 2 s) -> max-duration timer relay (60 s PE/N group, 10 s hold-to-run for F16) -> relay/Shelly contact -> coil (RC/MOV suppressed). Energise-to-fault wiring throughout; de-energised = correct installation, output off. Feedback: aux-contact blocks (Chint F4-11 / Hager ESC080 class) into Modbus DIs, isolated output-voltage transducers (ZMPT101B scaled ≥400 V) for L1/L2/L3-N and DUT-PE-vs-PE, F&F CKF-B/CP-730 (400 V-rated) as independent sequence/voltage confirmation, Pro 3EM/EM-50 currents; commanded vs actual compared within 500 ms, mismatch -> drop all coils + open main + latch. Firmware enforces the exclusion matrix (one fault per group, only composite = F16), duration table, arming preconditions (I_out <1 A for switching faults, supply 207-253 V and correct sequence, heatsink <60 °C, door closed, key in TEST), boost tap selection from measured supply so U_out ≤260 V, cycle counters for K_INT, return-to-normal verification before 'OK', pre-session self-test and SD logging. Network: isolated LAN switch + Shelly Pro LAN ports, ESP32 over Wi-Fi to a travel router (or ESP32 soft-AP fallback), Shelly AP/cloud off, digest auth or air-gapped; nothing safety-relevant depends on the network. Keep Shelly out of: 32 A paths, DC >30 V, PE switching, interlocks, and anything downstream of boost/N-open.
